$comment: Scoop manifest template. The release workflow substitutes 0.5.31,
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.31/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip and d03c12da3f98619dcfde24f2568a24dfaef064a379c14fe3f2b8fd1202d9bcb9 and commits the result to the bucket repository.
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.31/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip is on the public downloads CDN, never a GitHub release: this
repository is private, so a GitHub URL is a 404 for everyone who would
install from a public bucket. There is no `checkver`/`autoupdate` for the
same reason: the release workflow pushes the new manifest itself, and
the GitHub API it would poll is not open to the public either.
d03c12da3f98619dcfde24f2568a24dfaef064a379c14fe3f2b8fd1202d9bcb9 is read from the .sha256 the release publishes beside the
archive, the same one the patched PowerShell installer verifies against,
so there is exactly one published hash per archive.
post_install: Write-Host 'yoink installed. Run `yoink doctor` to check it over.'
